standard_prerequisites.name: The scheme theoretic support of a finite type quasi-coherent module and its local description by the annihilator, as defined and established in the morphisms chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies the scheme theoretic support and its support as a closed subset, which are two of the claims of the statement.

standard_prerequisites.name: The elementary properties of Fitting ideals, in particular that the zeroth Fitting ideal annihilates the module and that the closed subscheme it cuts out has the same underlying set as the support
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the scheme theoretic inclusion of the support in the Fitting subscheme and the equality of the two underlying closed subsets.

standard_prerequisites.name: The equivalence between quasi-coherent modules on a closed subscheme and quasi-coherent modules annihilated by the ideal sheaf, cited from the morphisms chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the finite type module on the Fitting subscheme whose pushforward is the given module.

core_obligations: Scheme theoretic inclusion: since the scheme theoretic support is locally cut out by the annihilator of the module, and the zeroth Fitting ideal is contained in that annihilator, the support is a closed subscheme of the subscheme cut out by the zeroth Fitting ideal (proof lines 1328-1334).

Equality of supports: the support of the module is the scheme theoretic support as a closed subset and the subscheme cut out by the zeroth Fitting ideal has the same underlying set as the support, so the three closed subsets coincide (proof lines 1336-1342).

The module on the Fitting subscheme: obtain the required finite type module either by pushing forward the module on the scheme theoretic support along the inclusion into the Fitting subscheme, or by applying the closed subscheme/module equivalence and the fact that the zeroth Fitting ideal annihilates the module (proof lines 1344-1349).
proof_roadmap: Compare the two closed subschemes through the annihilator and the zeroth Fitting ideal, getting the inclusion scheme theoretically and equality set theoretically (proof lines 1328-1342).
Produce the finite type module on the larger subscheme by pushing forward or by the closed subscheme/module equivalence (proof lines 1344-1349).
difficulty_reason: The lemma compares three closed subschemes attached to a finite type quasi-coherent module: the scheme theoretic support, the subscheme cut out by the zeroth Fitting ideal, and the support as a closed subset, and it adds that the module is pushed forward from the Fitting subscheme (statement lines 1309-1326). The counted proof is short but organises three separate points: the scheme theoretic inclusion from the elementary relation between the zeroth Fitting ideal and the annihilator, the equality of the underlying closed subsets from the corresponding property of Fitting ideals, and the existence of the required finite type module by pushing forward or by the closed subscheme/module equivalence (proof lines 1328-1349). It is H2: the argument is complete in the counted span and its inputs are the standard Fitting ideal and scheme theoretic support facts.
